subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what blocking/background/config boundaries should govern it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects user-visible reset latency, silent tool execution, memory retention, and plugin/config contracts, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Define a bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Approve an explicit reset-memory policy covering explicit, daily, and idle resets with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, and security constraints before implementation.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat hook/session-memory improvements such as #61675 as the supported reset boundary and close or narrow this issue away from silent agent execution.

options.title: Defer to external memory plugins
options.body: Require memory plugins or MCP-backed memory services to own continuous persistence and only extend core events where current plugin APIs are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit reset-memory policy covering explicit, daily, and idle resets with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, and security constraints before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the pre-compaction flush and /new reset history, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product decision.
